study_identification_part.si_4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study proposes and compares a Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model (HBLM) and a Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model (HBGPM) to account for site effects.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: In a hierarchical linear version of the model, site is modeled hierarchically, resulting in a random effect for site ('Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model, HBLM'). In a non-linear version of the model, a Gaussian Process for age is added... ('Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model, HBGPM').

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cortical thickness of 34 bilateral regions and average cortical thickness.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For the current study, we focused on cortical thickness measures of the 34 bilateral regions (averaged between left and right hemisphere) of the Desikian Killiany atlas parcellation... and the average cortical thickness across all 34 regions.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and Sex were used as fixed effects (covariates), and Site was used as a random effect.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: normative models describing the association between age, sex, and cortical thickness measures can be modeled... The ability of the model to deal with site effects is obtained by introducing a random effect for site...
